messages:
mikhail: Heads-up — us-east1 gnode pool is seeing a sustained write IOPS spike (~45k -> 130k) on local NVMe and SMART temps drifting up on a subset of hosts. This started right after the midnight cleaner concurrency bump. GPUs queued for attach are timing out. :eyes:
priya: Yikes. Any disk errors in dmesg or kernel logs?
alex: Seeing lots of writeback stalls on gnode-ue1-12 and gnode-ue1-19. /var/log/syslog shows repeated blk_mq timeouts.
mikhail: Logs: ```May 12 02:07:12 gnode-ue1-12 kernel: nvme0: I/O 0 QID 1 timeout, ABORTED``` Also cleaner job logs show a sudden rise in small-file deletions around 02:00 (correlates with the rollout).
devops-bot: Deploy: cleaner-concurrency v2.3.4 rolled to us-east1 at 2024-05-12T02:00Z by alex (canary=10%).
rachel: Can we throttle the cleaner on us-east1 or revert the concurrency change? If cleaner is causing tiny synchronous deletes, write amplification could be killing queue depth.
oncall-tim: I can temporarily pause the cleaner rollout for us-east1. Want me to flip it?
priya: Please pause the rollout and reduce concurrency to the previous value (2 -> 1) while we triage.
mikhail: Agreed. Also switch affected hosts to fallback path for GPU attaches: route attach requests to secondary scratchpool (read-only warm cache) to avoid attach failures.
oncall-tim: Pausing now. `deployctl rollback cleaner-concurrency --region us-east1 --to v2.3.3` -> in progress. :white_check_mark:
alex: After rollback started, I see attach queue length drop a bit. But some nodes still show sustained iops. Could be NVMe queues partially clogged; suggest invoking the per-host scrub backoff to drop background GC.
rachel: Can we evict pending cleaner shards from hot hosts? `kubectl -n infra scale job/cleaner-us-east1 --replicas=0` for hot nodes?
priya: Doing a controlled scale-down of cleaner pods in the affected AZ (az1 & az2). Running `kubectl patch` to annotate hosts to avoid scheduling cleaner pods.
mikhail: Also let's collect SMART + iostat samples for 30m and run `nvme fw-log` if temps keep rising. Post the attached sample here once done.
alex: Pasted iostat snippet: ```Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util nvme0 0.00 0.00 5.00 2100.00 8.00 42000.00 20.00 23.45 1.50 0.80 2.00 0.12 98.50``` Looks like tiny writes dominating.
rachel: If disk wear amplifies, we should consider temporarily shifting GPU scheduling away from the worst hosts. Can ops mark them cordoned for new GPU pods?
oncall-tim: Cordoning gnode-ue1-12 and gnode-ue1-19 now. Will drain with `--ignore-daemonsets` to avoid long pod preconditions.
mikhail: Next steps: 1) rollback concurrency (done), 2) scale down cleaner on affected AZs (in progress), 3) cordon + drain hottest hosts (in progress), 4) collect SMART + nvme logs, 5) fallback attach routing (planned). If attach success rate improves, we'll uncordon gradually.
priya: I've uploaded the nvme smartctl snapshot to the ops bucket: gs://redwood-ops/smart/us-east1/1715501234/*. Link: https://storage.redwood/smart/us-east1/1715501234/
alex: Question on long-term — the cleaner's small-delete pattern is generating high random writes. We should add an adaptive throttle based on iostat avgqu-sz and device temp thresholds. Lower priority for deletes when avgqu > 10.
mikhail: Good idea. Opening a follow-up RFC/issue. For now, we need triage telemetry: attach success rate, per-host iops, cleaner delete rate, seq vs random ratio.
rachel: After half an hour, attach failures dropped from 12/min to 1/min on fallback path. Rolling GPU launches resumed on unaffected hosts.
priya: Rollback fully completed at 02:22 UTC. Cleaner concurrency v2.3.3 pinned for us-east1 until patch lands.
oncall-tim: Monitoring for 1 hour; will escalate to paging if temps continue upward or error counts spike.
alex: Thanks all. Follow-up: I'll prototype a conservative cleaner mode (batch deletes + async unlink) and run it in canary.
mikhail: Nice. Adding this thread to the incident log. If anyone finds persistent SMART reallocation increases, ping me. :thumbsup:
